text:
Goyita of my soul,

far from you,

pain torments

my loving breast.

Ah! who could

receive in your arms

fierce death!

For to me

it would be sweeter

than my life

when absent from you.

It is bliss

to live and not see you,

sweet beauty!

Seeking here a gift

to consecrate to you,

I find nothing of my own

to give you;

for in my meadow

everything dies, Goyita,

if you are away.

There is a single plant

green and flourishing,

thanks to my watering it

evening and morning;

I cultivate it

because it is a memory of you,

a living portrait.

It bears a fruit sweeter

than bees’ bread,

and in sweetness it resembles

your laments of love;

your pleasant breath

is echoed by its perfume

that scents the wind—.

Goyita, there is only one

that I send you,

born in my orchards

in summer.

The sun gilds it,

for of all fruits it is

queen and lady.

Its green and gold

is not as beautiful

as that of your lip,

precious crimson;

and in the countryside

there is no tastier fruit,

for it is… the pineapple.

Do you remember that day,

loving Goya,

when your beautiful mouth

gave me pineapple;

and without offending you

I took the pineapple

that was on your lip?

I do not know whether the one now

my love sends you

will be as sweet

as that of that day.

Ah! if only I could

take it from your lips

even if I died!

translation.title: To Goyita
translation.editorial_note: The closing pineapple image is kept as both literal fruit and remembered kiss; “pan de abejas” is rendered as “bees’ bread” rather than replaced with a more specific honey term.
